# Results — Study 230 (Ohlson O-score) on real EDGAR + yfinance tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Ohlson O-score
computed annually from EDGAR 10-K fundamentals (fiscal year *t*). Forward
return = calendar year *t+1*. Panel: current S&P 500 members projected back —
**survivorship-biased**; results are upper bounds. As-of **2026-06-16**.*

O-score panel: **16 years × 241 tickers**, **2,474 valid firm-year observations**.

## The hedge in numbers

| Statistic | Value |
|---|--:|
| Hedge mean (safe − distressed) | **−4.45%/yr** |
| Hedge volatility | 11.48%/yr |
| Sharpe (annual) | −0.39 |
| Bootstrap 95% CI on Sharpe | [−1.07, +0.02] |
| **HAC t-stat** | **−1.59** |
| Hit rate (years with positive hedge) | 31% |
| n years | 16 |

## Per-bucket annual means

| Bucket | Mean return/yr | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| **Low-O (safe)** | +21.5% | +8.09 |
| Mid-O (grey zone) | +19.7% | — |
| **High-O (distressed)** | +26.0% | +8.72 |
| Market EW | +22.4% | — |

*The distressed (high-O) bucket earns more than the safe (low-O) bucket —
the **distress-premium direction** — but the HAC t-stat of −1.59 does not
clear the ±2 inference bar. This is consistent with the Altman-Z finding
(study 123): no reliable return-predictive signal from distress measures
in a survivorship-biased S&P 500 panel.*

## Survivorship-bias caveat

The EDGAR panel uses *current* S&P 500 membership projected backwards. Firms
that went bankrupt, were delisted, or exited the index between 2008 and 2023
are **absent** — which systematically inflates the high-O (distressed) bucket
returns. In reality, the most distressed firms — those most likely to default
and suffer near-zero or negative returns — are precisely the firms missing from
this panel. A live, unbiased implementation would find a weaker or negative
distress premium once bankrupt/delisted firms are included.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Hedge HAC t = −1.59, below the ±2 inference bar.
  Firm-level correlation = +0.048 (economically small). The O-score does not
  reliably separate winners from losers within this survivorship-biased S&P 500
  universe over 2008–2023.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The −4.45%/yr gross hedge (favouring distressed
  stocks) fails the inference bar and carries a heavy survivorship-bias
  haircut. Implementation cost and survivorship adjustment would eliminate
  any residual edge.
- **Distress premium direction present but noisy.** Contrary to Altman-Z
  (study 123), the O-score hedge leans toward the distress-premium direction
  (distressed firms earn more, not less) in this biased sample — but the
  t-stat is too weak to draw conclusions. The main lesson is the same: O-score
  is a bankruptcy predictor, not a reliable equity return predictor.
